topic: Training through a setback in the body: when we are sore, sick or nursing a niggle, the body can do less, but it does not choose for us; we rest the part that hurts and keep looking after the parts that still work, instead of writing the whole week off
figure: Epictetus, Stoic teacher c. 50-135 AD, a former slave who was lame (Enchiridion 9: illness is an impediment to the body but not to our choice, unless we will it; lameness is an impediment to the leg, not to our choice). Paraphrased, not quoted. Single quote page, at Mintra's request

lines: วันที่ร่างกายเจ็บหรือป่วย
เราทำได้น้อยลงจริง
แต่มันไม่ได้เลือกแทนเรา
พักส่วนที่เจ็บ
แล้วดูแลส่วนที่ยังทำได้
